units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
Terrible weather we have been having lately.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Follows him.
It's such blessed weather for the country, sir.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: No doubt; you are quite right. We townspeople give too little thought to that.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: He begins to take off his overcoat.
Oh, mayn't I help you?--There! Why, how wet it is? I'll just hang it up in the hall. And your umbrella, too--I'll open it and let it dry.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: She goes out with the things through the second door on the right.
PASTOR MANDERS takes off his travelling bag and lays it and his hat on a chair.
Meanwhile REGINA comes in again.
Ah, it's a comfort to get safe under cover. I hope everything is going on well here?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, thank you, sir.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: You have your hands full, I suppose, in preparation for to-morrow?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, there's plenty to do, of course.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: And Mrs. Alving is at home, I trust?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh dear, yes. She's just upstairs, looking after the young master's chocolate.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Yes, by-the-bye--I heard down at the pier that Oswald had arrived.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, he came the day before yesterday. We didn't expect him before to-day.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Quite strong and well, I hope?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, thank you, quite; but dreadfully tired with the journey. He has made one rush right through from Paris--the whole way in one train, I believe. He's sleeping a little now, I think; so perhaps we'd better talk a little quietly.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Sh!--as quietly as you please.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Arranging an arm-chair beside the table.
Now, do sit down, Pastor Manders, and make yourself comfortable.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: He sits down; she places a footstool under his feet.
There! Are you comfortable now, sir?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Thanks, thanks, extremely so.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Looks at her.
Do you know, Miss Engstrand, I positively believe you have grown since I last saw you.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Do you think so, Sir? Mrs. Alving says I've filled out too.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Filled out? Well, perhaps a little; just enough.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Short pause.
Shall I tell Mrs. Alving you are here?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Thanks, thanks, there is no hurry, my dear child.--By-the-bye, Regina, my good girl, tell me: how is your father getting on out here?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh, thank you, sir, he's getting on well enough.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: He called upon me last time he was in town.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Did he, indeed? He's always so glad of a chance of talking to you, sir.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: And you often look in upon him at his work, I daresay?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: I? Oh, of course, when I have time, I--
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Your father is not a man of strong character, Miss Engstrand. He stands terribly in need of a guiding hand.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh, yes; I daresay he does.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: He requires some one near him whom he cares for, and whose judgment he respects. He frankly admitted as much when he last came to see me.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, he mentioned something of the sort to me. But I don't know whether Mrs. Alving can spare me; especially now that we've got the new Orphanage to attend to. And then I should be so sorry to leave Mrs. Alving; she has always been so kind to me.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: But a daughter's duty, my good girl--Of course, we should first have to get your mistress's consent.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: But I don't know whether it would be quite proper for me, at my age, to keep house for a single man.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: What! My dear Miss Engstrand! When the man is your own father!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, that may be; but all the same--Now, if it were in a thoroughly nice house, and with a real gentleman--
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Why, my dear Regina--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: --one I could love and respect, and be a daughter to--
units.name: REGINA
